checked.comment: Stochastic i.i.d. losses in [0,1]^K; T is assumed known; Theorem 1 assumes a unique optimal arm.
Losses may depend on the history of losses and chosen arms, so the adversary is adaptive. Losses lie in [0,1].
The corruption level C is defined as an expectation, and regret is measured on the corrupted losses. Both are recorded correctly.
Lower-bound setting for consistent algorithms with losses in [0,1].
Matches eq. thm1-bound-sto. The o(log T) remainder is handled as limsup, as instruction 21 requires.
Matches eq. thm1-bound-adv: the leading constant is 1 and only the K log T term is inside O().
Matches Theorem 1's statement for the corrupted setting, R + O(sqrt(C R)), which Proposition 3 repeats.

Matches Proposition 1's expression. This is a simplification, derived in the paper, of the bound of Honda & Takemura (2012). Recording it as a result is acceptable because the paper derives the simplified form itself.
Matches the corrupted-setting bound for the modified algorithm in Remark 1.

missing_results.description: Precise limsup bound on R(T)/log T in stochastic settings for the proposed algorithm, in terms of the explicit function h(sigma_i^2/Delta_i) plus 2(1+eps). This is sharper than the max{4z + c log(1+z), 2(1+eps)} form in Theorem 1.

summary: The extraction is accurate. The settings, expressions, constants and qualifiers for Theorem 1 (stochastic, adversarial and corrupted cases), Remark 1 and Proposition 1 all match the source, and both algorithms map to the right registry entries. The only gap is Proposition 2: it gives the stochastic limsup bound in terms of the function h, which is a different expression from Theorem 1's, and the extraction mentions it only in the notes of r1.
